candidates.title: Business report to video in n8n: your monthly numbers, explained by Claude in 2 minutes (free n8n workflow template)

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare a narrated video from a monthly business review report for a team, board, or client.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: if you send your team, your investors or your clients a review deck every month

ease.reason: A supplied report and audience fields can support a small sample video draft, but render setup is not trivial.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: client-facing firms may value a faster monthly review video; the post offers a workflow, not buying intent.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic report-to-script storyboard is bounded; real rendering and reliable figures remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A draft can repeat from a supplied report, but a person must verify figures, narration, and final render.

evidence.reason: The retained spans describe monthly review decks and a video workflow; broader demand and recurring use are not established.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable narration script and scene outline from an operator-supplied monthly review report.
inputs: Synthetic monthly report with labeled metrics
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a completed monthly review report and requests a video draft.
steps: Read the supplied report and audience notes.
Extract only labeled metrics and stated conclusions.
Draft a short narration and matching scene outline.
Compare each numeric statement with the supplied report.
Return the draft for a person to revise and approve.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fixed synthetic report, every metric in the draft must match its source row and each conclusion must be traceable to supplied text.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies accurate report data, checks interpretation and branding, and approves any render or client delivery.
unverified: Whether a video script can be generated accurately for varied report formats.
Whether customers want this output or would pay for it.
Any actual video rendering, workflow execution, or delivery capability.

candidates.reason: Assessed as a bounded proposed experiment; provisional criterion mean is below the frozen 6 threshold, and the source does not establish a paying customer.

candidates.title: AI chatbots, WhatsApp agents and booking automations for small businesses

demandEvidence.chore: Review workflow records to find scenarios that send duplicate records or miss records.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Fixing scenarios that send duplicates or miss records

ease.reason: A synthetic expected-versus-actual row comparison is easy to sketch, but no matching implementation reference is supplied.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small service firms may value record-fault review; this service listing does not establish buyer intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic comparison is bounded; real scenario data and reliable diagnosis remain unknown.

autonomy.reason: A comparison can flag differences, but a person must diagnose causes and approve changes.

evidence.reason: The retained span explicitly offers fixing duplicate or missed records, but gives no case detail or recurrence.

experimentPlan.output: A short exception list showing supplied workflow records that are missing or duplicated against an operator-defined expected list.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator provides an expected list and a captured output list for one workflow run.
steps: Read both supplied lists without connecting to a live workflow.
Apply the operator’s exact matching and duplicate rules.
List missing, repeated, and unmatched IDs.
Show the source rows for each flagged difference.
Ask a person to diagnose causes and approve any change.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a hand-built test pair, the output must flag every seeded missing or duplicate ID and leave all other IDs unflagged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person defines the matching rules, supplies authorized test records, investigates causes, and approves any live workflow change.
unverified: Whether synthetic comparison generalizes to any particular workflow data format.
Whether a live Make scenario can be read or changed.
Whether the listed service reflects recurring customer demand.

candidates.reason: Assessed as a bounded proposed experiment; provisional criterion mean is below the frozen 6 threshold, and the source does not establish a paying customer.

candidates.title: Feature request: Product-specific customer tax exemptions for accurate wholesale and retail checkout

demandEvidence.chore: Calculate tax amounts before payment and record GST and PST amounts accurately in Shopify order records and tax reports.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Calculate the correct tax amounts before payment, without requiring draft orders, manual adjustments or additional invoices.

ease.reason: A tax review worksheet can be outlined, but a correct calculation depends on jurisdiction and transaction rules not supplied here.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: wholesale and retail merchants may value fewer manual tax adjustments; this request does not prove willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A fictional case worksheet is bounded, but validating tax rules or producing correct amounts is outside the evidence.

autonomy.reason: A person would need to determine tax treatment and verify every result; automation could misstate tax.

evidence.reason: The retained task and context state a specific checkout and recordkeeping problem, but provide no rule details or corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: A manual-review checklist that identifies which operator-supplied exemption fields need review before a tax decision.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits one fictional wholesale or retail checkout case for review.
steps: Read only fictional case fields supplied by the operator.
Check whether required fields are present.
List missing or conflicting fields without calculating tax.
Link each flag to the supplied rule reference.
Return the case to a qualified person for decision.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a small synthetic set, the checklist must flag each intentionally missing required field and make no tax amount or eligibility decision.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A qualified person supplies authoritative rules, determines exemptions and tax amounts, and approves any production handling; no real customer records are used.
unverified: Applicable tax law and jurisdiction-specific rules.
Whether a field checklist materially reduces the stated manual work.
Any Shopify integration, tax calculation, or order-record persistence.

candidates.reason: Assessed as a bounded proposed experiment; provisional criterion mean is below the frozen 6 threshold, and the source does not establish a paying customer.

candidates.title: Make.com Automation for Simple Business Tasks

demandEvidence.chore: Connect a supplied Google Form response to a Google Sheet and prepare an automatic Gmail notification for review.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Connecting Google Forms to Google Sheets

ease.reason: A synthetic form-to-sheet mapping is approachable, though no supplied implementation reference documents the proposed flow.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small professional firms may pay for setup help; this learner’s service offer does not show an established buyer.

feasibility.reason: A test using fictional form rows is bounded; permissions, delivery, and error handling are unverified.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable mapping and notification can be outlined, but a person must authorize access and review messages.

evidence.reason: The retained span lists concrete automation examples, but frames them as a builder’s offer rather than demonstrated customer demand.

experimentPlan.output: A review sheet mapping fictional form requests to selected columns and a notification draft for each row.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a new fictional form response row for processing.
steps: Read the supplied test row and mapping.
Check required fields and mark missing values.
Place mapped values in a proposed sheet row.
Draft a notification using the approved template.
Show both outputs to a person before any send.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For seeded fictional rows, mapped values must land in their selected columns and notifications must contain only the approved fields.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person configures and authorizes real accounts, checks mappings, reviews each message, and approves any send.
unverified: Whether any integration executes successfully in Make.
Whether permissions, retries, and duplicate handling are available.
Whether the offered task represents repeated buyer demand.

candidates.reason: Assessed as a bounded proposed experiment; provisional criterion mean is below the frozen 6 threshold, and the source does not establish a paying customer.

candidates.title: Coordinate opt-in merchant research conversations

demandEvidence.chore: Help app developers find store owners for short research conversations about how merchants work and where they struggle.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: one of the hardest parts has been finding store owners to talk to.

ease.reason: A consent-based outreach tracker can be prototyped with supplied fictional prospects, but the source does not identify effective merchant channels.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: Shopify app developers may value better merchant research outreach; this post does not show willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can draft and track invitations from operator-supplied opt-in leads; reliable lead discovery is unresolved.

autonomy.reason: The tracker can prepare follow-ups, but a person must find eligible prospects, obtain consent, and conduct conversations.

evidence.reason: The post says finding store owners for short research conversations is difficult; it gives no tested channel or recurring volume.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable outreach queue with a tailored invitation draft and consent/status fields for each operator-supplied prospective merchant.
inputs: Fictional prospect record with a public opt-in contact route
App problem description supplied by the developer
Research purpose and proposed conversation length
experimentPlan.trigger: The app developer supplies an eligible prospect and requests a research invitation draft.
steps: Check that the prospect record includes an operator-verified public opt-in route.
Draft a short invitation from the supplied research purpose and approved wording.
Place the invitation and consent status in a review queue.
Have the developer verify relevance and approve any outreach.
Record replies and schedule only conversations the merchant accepts.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For synthetic prospect records, each draft must use only supplied facts, include the stated research purpose, and remain unsent until a person approves it; declined or unknown consent must not be queued for follow-up.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The developer must find prospects through appropriate channels, verify contact permissions, approve every message, and conduct the conversation; the proposal does not automate access to merchants or send outreach.
unverified: Which channels can reliably reach store owners willing to speak with app developers.
Whether this workflow reduces the stated difficulty or supports repeated conversations.
Whether app developers would pay for outreach coordination.
Any integration, delivery, response tracking, or scheduling capability.

candidates.reason: The discussion explicitly says finding store owners for short conversations about how merchants work and struggle is difficult. A consent-based outreach tracker is a bounded experiment, but the post gives no effective channel, repeat frequency, or buyer evidence; provisional mean is below 6.
